acceptance_criteria.criterion: AC6: handleListDialogues() returns an empty dialogues: [] array when ?wp= is provided with a value not matching /^WP-\d+$/
AC7: Valid ?wp=WP-001 values continue to work as before
AC8: A test in api.test.ts covers the invalid ?wp= case
AC9: A console.warn() or console.error() call is emitted when the regex check rejects a filename

summary: Added WP_ID_RE constant (/^WP-\\d+$/) and wpId validation to handleListDialogues() in mcp-server/gui/api.ts — invalid wpId returns [] without error. Added console.warn() calls on both rejection paths in handleGetDialogueFile(): regex allowlist check and prefix (path traversal) check; both log messages include the rejected filename. Added 4 new tests in tests/gui/api.test.ts (AC6, AC7, AC9/AC11/AC12, AC10/AC11/AC12). All 332 GUI tests pass. Note: AC9 (regex check) and AC10 (prefix check) are both validated, though the prefix check is unreachable in practice from the regex rejection path — the regex covers all filesystem traversal attempts before the prefix check.

comments.note: The prefix (path traversal) check in handleGetDialogueFile is effectively unreachable after the regex check — any path traversal attempt is caught by the regex first. The defense-in-depth prefix check is still valuable but the separate console.warn test for it uses the same scenario as the regex check.
No observations — code is clean and consistent with existing style.

summary: All 7 acceptance criteria (AC6–AC12) verified. 1678/1678 tests pass across 58 test files. WP_ID_RE constant and validation logic are correctly implemented in handleListDialogues(). console.warn() calls with filename in log message are present on both rejection paths in handleGetDialogueFile(). New WP-003 labelled tests cover AC6 (invalid wpId returns []), AC7 (valid WP-001 filter still works), and AC9/AC11/AC12 + AC10/AC11/AC12 (console.warn spy confirms filename is logged). No regressions.

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent with existing api.ts style. WP_ID_RE constant is well-placed and clearly documented.
AC6 test is thorough: it checks 5 invalid wpId values ('../etc', 'WP-', 'WP-abc', 'not-a-wp-id', ' WP-001') and asserts each returns []. This covers both injection attempts and malformed inputs.

AC10 test uses '../secret.md' which triggers the regex check (not the prefix check path). The prefix check code with console.warn IS present in api.ts (line 1312), but the test does not independently exercise it because the regex allowlist makes the prefix path unreachable in practice. The AC is satisfied at the implementation level (the warn is there); the test title is slightly misleading but functionally correct as a defense-in-depth confirmation.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (mcp-server/gui/api.ts, mcp-server/tests/gui/api.test.ts). All OWASP Top 10 categories evaluated. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 1 Info observation (assertSafeSlug denylist pattern, pre-existing). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01 (Broken Access Control) PASS: handleGetDialogueFile() implements two-layer path traversal defence. Layer 1: DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE allowlist (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.md$/) at api.ts line 1302 — rejects any filename containing '/', '.', '..', or non-alphanumeric characters. Layer 2: resolve() + startsWith(dialoguesDir + '/') prefix check at api.ts line 1311 — defence-in-depth for hypothetical allowlist bypass on unusual filesystems. Both layers are correctly implemented. ✅

A01 (Broken Access Control) PASS: handleListDialogues() validates the optional wpId query parameter against WP_ID_RE (/^WP-\d+$/) at api.ts line 1265 before using it as a filename prefix filter. Malformed or injection-attempt values silently return [] rather than propagating to the filesystem. The prefix is used only in a String.startsWith() call (no filesystem access), so even an unvalidated value could not escape the directory — but the validation adds correctness and prevents unexpected filter behaviour. ✅

INFO — A01 (Broken Access Control): assertSafeSlug() at api.ts line 90 uses a denylist pattern (checks for '/' and '..' substrings) rather than a full allowlist regex. This is a pre-existing pattern not introduced by this WP. In context it is sufficient (the ledger slug is also constrained by the filesystem), but a future hardening could replace it with a strict allowlist (e.g. the existing SAFE_SLUG_REGEX constant imported from constants.js). No new risk introduced.

A09 (Security Logging) PASS: console.warn() calls on both rejection paths in handleGetDialogueFile() (api.ts lines 1303, 1312) include the rejected filename in the log message. This provides an audit trail for path traversal attempts. Test coverage via vi.spyOn(console, 'warn') confirms the log messages fire correctly (tests/gui/api.test.ts lines 1383–1413). ✅

No security findings at Critical or High severity — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. Input validation is robust (allowlist regex + defence-in-depth prefix check). The wpId injection vector is correctly mitigated. Security sign-off: PASS.

summary: WP_ID_RE constant (/^WP-\d+$/) is well-named, correctly anchored (^ and $), and placed alongside DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE in the same constants block. JSDoc comment accurately describes intent.

handleListDialogues() wpId validation (lines 1264–1270): guard correctly placed before the prefix filter, returns [] on invalid input without throwing. Code reads cleanly and the early-return idiom is consistent with the rest of the file.

handleGetDialogueFile() two-layer defence (lines 1302–1314): Layer 1 DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE allowlist correctly rejects any filename with '/', '.', spaces, or non-alphanumeric characters; Layer 2 resolve+startsWith is a correct defence-in-depth pattern. Both rejection paths emit console.warn() with the filename in the log message — satisfying AC9, AC10, AC11.

The prefix check (layer 2) is functionally unreachable via the regex (layer 1) on all standard POSIX/Windows filesystems. The code is still correct and valuable as defence-in-depth; the test for AC10 re-uses the regex-rejection scenario as a pragmatic acknowledgement of this. The test comment at line 1395–1413 explains this clearly — transparent and acceptable.

api.test.ts WP-003 tests: AC6 covers 5 distinct invalid wpId values (injection, empty, malformed) — thorough. AC7 confirms the happy path is unbroken. AC9/AC12 and AC10/AC12 tests use vi.spyOn(console, 'warn') with mockRestore() in a finally block — correct cleanup pattern.
All 7 ACs (AC6–AC12) confirmed met. No regressions — 1,678 tests pass. Code review: PASS.

comments.note: api.ts line 1311 — the prefix check condition is `!filePath.startsWith(dialoguesDir + '/') && filePath !== dialoguesDir`. The second conjunct (`filePath !== dialoguesDir`) guards the edge case where the filename resolves to exactly the dialogues directory itself. Given that DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE requires a .md extension this edge case is already impossible, but the guard is harmless and makes the intent explicit. No change needed.

api.test.ts line 1395–1413 — the AC10 test title ('prefix check rejects') describes a code path that is unreachable in practice. The comment block explains this correctly. Consider a follow-up task to rename the test or add a note pointing to the implementation comment, so future maintainers understand why the test uses the same stimulus as AC9.
No further observations — implementation is clean, idiomatic, and consistent with established api.ts conventions. Code review: PASS.
